reuse.why: Extends the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and RSchedule/recurConfigToRSchedule, but getDatesInRange rebuilds the daily-skip check inline (d.isWeekend || isHoliday) instead of reusing a shared non-working-day/daily-skip decision, and the private isNonWorkingDay is not exported for it.

duplication.why: The 'daily + skipWeekend -> drop non-working occurrences' rule is written in getNextDate (twice, forward and reverse filter) and again in getDatesInRange, and schedule-template now passes skipWeekend into the helper while still keeping its own skipWeekend ternary.

placement.why: Holiday/weekend adjustment correctly lives in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip policy is split between shared getNextDate and the server handler rather than owned by one shared function.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the schedule date logic, the new handler, types and tests; the solve-mode error check reshuffle is minor incidental churn.

maintainability.why: Weekend/holiday moving is centralised, but the daily-skip rule exists in several divergent places (getUpcomingDates and the budget template do not apply it at all), so future rule changes must be hunted down.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange re-implements the non-working-day test (d.isWeekend || isHoliday) and daily-skip decision instead of going through shared/schedules.ts; budget/schedule-template.ts keeps its own dateConditions.value.skipWeekend ternary around getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange's `isDaily && skipWeekend && (d.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(...))` is a reshaped copy of getNextDate's isDailyWithSkippedWeekends + isNonWorkingDay filter.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains daily-skip special branches on both the forward and reverse occurrence paths; getDatesInRange re-implements the daily-skip/non-working test and schedule-template keeps its own skipWeekend gate while also passing the flag.
